Good afternoon and good morning, everyone – and thank you for your interest 
in bp’s full year 2025 results . I am delighted
 to welcome our guests in the 
room, and those on the webcast . 
I’m joined today by Carol Howle, interim chief executive officer ; Kate Thomson, 
chief financial officer ; and Gordon Birrell, executive vice president Production
 
and Operations
.
Before I handover to Carol, let me draw your attention to our cautionary
 
statement .

Thank you Craig .
It’s a real privilege to be here as Interim CEO ahead of Meg O’Neill’s arrival as 
chief executive officer in April . On behalf of the entire bp team, I’d also like to 
take the opportunity
 to thank Murray for his 34 years of service, his leadership
 
and contributions
 to the company .   
Stepping back for a moment ... 
As we started 2025 it was clear to us that this was a year of turnaround
. We had 
not been performing
 as strongly as we should have been, and that required 
urgent and focused intervention
. We have made good progress
 in 2025 to 
address that . 
Kate, Gordon and I will spend around 30 minutes talking through our 
performance,
 highlights
 and delivery of our plan .
And we know we have more to do – to accelerate
 delivery and to position the 
company for the future opportunities
 we have ahead of us . 
The team and I have conviction
 in our potential to deliver significant
 growth in 
shareholder
 value .
From my 25 years in bp, I know we have fantastic
 assets and exceptional
 
people . Our strategic
 direction is right, we have made a good start in delivering
 
against the plan laid out 12 months ago and I just want to thank everyone at bp 
for what we’ve delivered . 
And we look forward to Meg joining as CEO – she is an outstanding
 
leader, and together as a leadership
 team we will continue to drive 
our strategy forward in accelerating
 the turnaround
 of this great 
company .

Kate ran through some of the highlights
 on the video at 7am .  So, I’ll just 
recap a few of them .
Our operational
 performance
 was strong across the group . 
Reported upstream production
 was lower than 2024 , which reflected
 
portfolio changes . Underlying
 production
 was held broadly flat, which 
exceeded our annual guidance 12 months ago .  
We set new records in upstream plant reliability
 and refining availability,
 
with both above 96 % for the year . 
We started up seven major projects and our reserves replacement
 ratio was 
90 % - up from an average of around 50 % in the previous two years .
Based on provisional
 data, our operational
 emissions
 in 2025 were 37% less 
than in 2019 – a reduction well in excess of our target of 20 %.  
Our supply trading and shipping business remains a distinctive
 competitive
 
advantage
 for bp – delivering
 an average around 4% uplift to bp’s returns, 
which now extends over the last six years . 
We concluded
 the strategic
 review of Castrol with an agreement
 to sell a 
65 % shareholding
. We believe the sale – and the retention of a position in 
Castrol – represents
 a very good outcome for shareholders
. It allows us to 
realise value today while continuing
 to benefit from future growth of that 
5
business .
And in one year we have completed
 and announced
 over $11 billion 
of our planned $20 billion divestment
 programme
.
Let me turn now to safety, our number one priority .

Our commitment
 to our safety goals is unwavering
 is to eliminate fatalities, 
life changing
 injuries and Tier 1 process safety events across our operations
.
Tragically,
 in 2025 , four colleagues
 lost their lives while working in our US 
retail business . Two were killed in separate incidents where they were struck 
by passing vehicles as they carried out emergency
 roadside assistance
. In 
response, we have permanently
 stopped roadside assistance
 next to active 
traffic lanes - a decision made solely to protect the safety of our people . Our 
thoughts remain with the families, friends and colleagues
 of the four people 
who lost their lives .
On process safety, we have seen encouraging
 progress
. Combined
 Tier 1 and 2 
events are down by around a third compared with the previous year . 
While process safety has improved, we recognise
 we have more to do . We 
must learn from every incident and every challenge
 to keep us safe today and 
tomorrow .

Turning then to our primary targets, where we have made good progress
 this 
year . Kate will provide further details on each of the four shortly, but the 
headlines are ;
—We increased
 adjusted free cash flow by around 55 % in 2025 , on a price 
adjusted basis . 
—Net debt at the end of 2025 was $22.2 billion, $800 million lower than at the 
end of 2024 . 
—We have now delivered $2.8 billion of our $4 to 5 billion structural
 cost 
reduction target since the start of the programme,
 including
 around $2 
billion in 2025 . Going forward, we have increased
 this target to $5.5 to 6.5 
billion, which includes the expected cost reductions
 from the divestment
 of 
Castrol . Kate will cover this shortly .
—And return on average capital employed was around 14% in 2025 , on a price 
adjusted basis – that’s up from around 12% in 2024 . 
We are executing
 our plan, taking decisive action on costs, capital and 
portfolio . Combined
 with the board’s decision to suspend the share buyback 
and fully allocate excess cash to the balance sheet, this will create a strong 
platform to invest with discipline
 into our deep hopper of oil & gas 
opportunities
.
In the near term, this is supported
 by three more major projects that we 
7
expect to bring online by the end of 2027 . With six more projects 
sanctioned,
 we are on track to bring a further eight to ten projects 
online between 2028 and 2030 . 
As we look to the long term, our success
 in exploration
 and access 
in 2025 has created a real sense of excitement
 around the company 
and the opportunities
 ahead of us, including
 in the Middle East, 
Brazil and Namibia . And, there is more to come, with planned 
exploration
 wells this year, including
 in Libya, Angola, Brazil and the 
Gulf of America . 
We see potential to drive disciplined
 organic production
 growth 
over the longer term, underpinned
 by our distinctive
 resource 
hopper and our capability
 – our people, our technology,
 our 
experience
 – and that will maximise value for our shareholders
.  
More on that from Gordon shortly, as well as the significant
 
progress
 being made by the team in the downstream,
 which I’ll 
come back to later . But, for now, let me hand over to Kate .

Thanks Carol and good afternoon, everyone . 
We covered our fourth quarter and full year results in the video released earlier 
today at 7am UK time, so I will just do a quick recap of the headlines here . 
—We generated
 underlying
 replacement
 cost profit, or net income, of $7.5 
billion in 2025 , against the backdrop
 of a weaker price environment
. This 
result was underpinned
 by strong operating performance
 which Carol 
already highlighted
. 
—Operating
 cashflow for the year was $24.5 billion, including
 an adjusted 
working capital build of $2.9 billion this year . We improved capital efficiency
 
and tightened further our discipline,
 delivering
 full year capex of $14.5 billion, 
including a reduction of organic capex to $13.6 billion .
—For 2025 , including
 the fourth quarter dividend announced
 this morning, 
shareholder
 distributions
 for the year were around 30 % of our 2025 
operating cash flow and within the guidance issued last February . As 
mentioned in this morning’s release, the guidance for shareholder
 
distributions
 is now retired . The dividend remains our first financial priority .
As we guided in our trading statement,
 we recognised
 impairments
 of around 
$4 billion after tax this quarter . These impairment
 charges are related largely to 
our transition businesses,
 including
 biogas and renewables,
 where we took 
decisive action to manage our pace of growth and high -grade our portfolio to
